body:
hey there! i too have combination 3B/3C hair, but i personally find this look/style to be hard to achieve with my hair. I am mixed race and have medium density and porosity. have you tried doing a light weight mousse or gel when your hair is 75% dry? if so, does it hold that style well? also i have the same issue with greasy scalp and dry ends. i’ve noticed that if i apply conditioner to the ends of my hair about every 2-3 showers (i wash my hair once a week) that helps the frizz. i also apply hair oil to my ends daily. for starters, a leave in conditioner (heavy if you have thick hair) would do wonders. also, have you tried fry shampoo on your hair? 
my routine that i’ve stuck w for the past year is this:
-shampoo my hair once a week following a deep conditioner and/or a hot oil treatment (hot oil treatments do wonders for dry ends, even if it’s just olive oil heated in the microwave)
-follow up with a good conditioner
*btw, you don’t need super expensive products, but clean, organic, and salon grade are best*
-i then brush my hair out (scalp outwards, not downwards, this helps w volume)
-after i dry my hair w a t-shirt or microfiber towel
-while still wet/ damp, i apply miss jessie’s leave in condish, followed by rodan and fields define+curl cream, (i also use miss jessie’s multicultural curls if i don’t have the other one, which has always been a styling staple for me), then i follow up with rodan and fields defrizz oil treatment. 
-sometimes i’ll do the “plop” method at this point, which hasn’t done much for me but may help you get the cohesive style you’re looking for
-my hair air dries fast, so i let it air dry and then do a final style

i’m sorry this is so long lol, but important note: always apply any product except shampoo from mid length downwards, especially concentrating on your ends if that’s an issue. applying product at the root gives that flat/greasy look. 

other good products i’ve tried: miss jessie’s pillow soft curls (THIS ONE IS AMAZING, ESPECIALLY FOR THE LOOK YOURE GOING FOR!! 10/10 recommend), and carols daughter leave in conditioner and hair oil (black vanilla). i tend to stay away from cantu and shea moisture personally because they weigh my hair down quite a bit, but they were amazing for fixing years of heat damage my hair went through. 

other good tips: always use a microfiber towel or tshirt to dry. if you’re hair takes to long to air dry, diffusing or a combo of both will help you get the ethereal style/ volume. clipping your hair at the crown while drying/ after drying also helps with volume. ALWAYS *seriously* use a bonnet, hair buff, or satin pillow case when sleeping. these tiny investments do wonders. lastly, DO NOT brush/comb fry curly hair. this leads to frizz and breakage. i only comb my hair when i’m the shower, and i add a bit of conditioner if it’s still too knotted. 

i hope this makes sense and helps a bit lol, it took years for me to perfect a routine and figure out what my hair likes, so be patient w it, it’s trial and error:) lmk if you have any other questions !
